corrections.issue: Date misread. Oppenheimer says the Fed 'finally gave up the language of transitory really at the beginning of last year'; the interview is dated October 2022, so this is 2021 as he speaks (in fact the Fed retired the word in Nov-Dec 2021), not the start of 2022.
corrections.fix: Central banks called inflation transitory for a long time and dropped that language only about a year before the interview (he says 'the beginning of last year'), so they were slow to turn hawkish.

completeness_estimate: 0.90 - first reader captured nearly every argument (bear-market taxonomy, bottom conditions, growth/value reversal, dollar, UK, commodities); missed only the inflation-as-tax mechanism, a few host remarks, UK linkers and the virtual-to-physical shift.
